title: FCS built from 0/1 flags
found: The workbook maps the FCS items of this round to jour_conso_* variables. Their labels ask for days, but the main groups hold only 0 or 1 (cereals are 1 for all 271 households). The FCS averages 11.9 and every household is Poor, while the analysts' SCA in the same file averages 53.2.
handling: Do not use this round's FCS and FCS groups. The main-group day counts cannot be rebuilt from this file (dep_ and auto_ are money values), so use the analysts' SCA, or ask WFP for the original counts.

title: rCSIBorrow points to the wrong column
found: The workbook maps rCSIBorrow to the rCSILessQlty column, although each raw file has its own rCSIBorrow. Borrowing has weight 2, so the rCSI is overstated: 9.10 instead of 7.59, 5.48 instead of 4.63, 5.89 instead of 4.89. With the true column, the result equals the analysts' rCSI for 100% of households.
handling: Correct these three cells of the workbook and rerun Rmd 06 and the do-file.

title: Coping scale left unrecoded
found: This file's labels are 1 = Yes, 2 = No need, 3 = Already exhausted, while the common scale is 1 = No need, 2 = Already exhausted, 3 = Yes. Rmd 05 relabels the codes without recoding them, so No need counts as coping. Emergency coping reads 56.7%; recoded, 5.8%.
handling: Recode this round as 2021 PDM is recoded (1 to 3, 2 to 1, 3 to 2), then rerun Rmd 05 and the do-file.

title: Raw coping code 0 becomes Yes
found: Rmd 05 recodes raw 0 to Yes in eight strategies. 0 is labelled Non in 2018, and the 111 households with 0 in 2020 PDM answer 0 to every strategy. Emergency coping: 2018 reads 29.6%, 21.2% if 0 is No; 2020 PDM reads 49.4%, 8.5% if 0 is No. In 2018 LhCSIStress1 already treats 0 as No, so the rule is not consistent.
handling: Confirm the meaning of 0 with the questionnaire or WFP, then apply one rule to all strategies.

title: Asset benefit score is 0 for a whole round
found: The labels of this file say 1 = Non, 2 = Oui, but the answers are coded 0 and 1, like the other rounds. Rmd 07 follows the labels and recodes 1 to 0, so all 1,701 scores are 0. The raw answers imply a mean of 5.8, in line with the other rounds.
handling: Treat 1 as Yes in this round (check with WFP), then rerun Rmd 07 and the do-file.

title: A coping strategy is emptied
found: LhCSIStress1 (selling non-productive assets) has answers in all raw files, but in the merged file it is 4 (Not applicable) for all households except in 2019 Annual. Stress and no-coping shares are affected; crisis and emergency shares are not. The exact line in Rmd 05 where the values are lost has not been isolated.
handling: Trace the variable through Rmd 05, then rerun it and the do-file.

title: No sampling weights
found: None of the 305 columns of the merged file is a weight, so every figure on this dashboard is unweighted. The surveys monitor WFP's programme areas: the figures describe the households surveyed, not the population of Chad or of a region.
handling: Do not read figures as population estimates. Add weights if WFP can provide them.

title: The sample changes between rounds
found: Regions enter and leave: Wadi Fira goes from 629 households in 2018 to 11 in 2023 PDM and none in 2023 Annual; Ennedi Est appears only in 2023 Annual; Sila is absent from 2021 PDM to 2022 Annual. Changes between rounds can come from who was surveyed.
handling: Compare the same regions when possible. Overview warns when the regions of two compared rounds differ.

title: Two survey seasons
found: PDMs take place in the lean season (July to September) and annual surveys after the harvest (November to February). Comparing consecutive rounds mixes the season with the change. The fieldwork of the 2020 and 2021 annual surveys ran into the next year.
handling: This dashboard compares each round with the previous one of the same series only.

title: Unlabelled coping codes
found: The codes in this file have no value labels. The pipeline reads 1 = No need and 3 = Yes, but the answers look like the 1 = Yes, 2 = No need scale of the following rounds: code 2 is by far the most common. On that scale, emergency coping would be 14.6%, not 23.6%.
handling: Check against the 2019 questionnaire. Flagged in both views, as the corrections do not change this round.

title: Impossible household sizes
found: 89 households have more than 30 members, up to 352 (333 boys aged 0 to 5 months in one household). 2022 PDM averages 11.9 members, 7.0 without them. 60 households in several rounds have a size of 0.
handling: Set a rule for these values before any per capita calculation. The indicative corrections leave out sizes above 30.

title: Crisis coping has fewer strategies early on
found: LhCSICrisis1 (selling productive assets) has no source in the first five rounds, so crisis coping rests on two strategies there and three after.
handling: Keep this in mind when comparing crisis coping across the 2021 Annual survey.

title: MAD and MDDW stay out of the merged file
found: Rmds 09 and 10 build these modules, but the do-file merges only nine modules. They hold one row per child or woman (3,371 and 9,923 rows), not one per household, so a 1:1 merge on ID is not possible. In most rounds the module files also hold more rows than the raw repeat files (for example 645 against 389 for MAD in 2021 Annual), which is not explained yet.
handling: Decide whether to add them: as household-level summaries, or as separate files. Check the extra rows first.

title: Combined assistance items
found: The first rounds ask about combined items (lean-season food or cash; blanket feeding of children or women; malnutrition treatment), split from 2021 Annual. No single series runs through the change. 2018 has no assistance question.
handling: Compare interventions within each period, or build a common grouping.

title: Answers are not comparable across assistance rounds
found: The share answering Yes to cash for assets is 98% and 99% in 2019 Annual and 2020 PDM, against 68% to 94% later. Early samples may have targeted participants.
handling: Do not read these shares as coverage rates without the sampling design.

title: Report table differs from the data
found: 12 cells of Table 1 of the Issues report differ from the merged file. For example, the report shows the combined school item from 2021 Annual to 2023 Annual, but it has answers only in 2020 PDM.
handling: Update the table. The Assistance page lists the 12 cells.
where: Issues on WFP Resilience Interventions in Chad, 2018-2023 datasets.docx

title: Fragile ID in PDM 2022
found: The raw file has no household ID, so each Rmd assigns the row number. The IDs still line up in the current files, tested on the raw rows, but any change of row order or filter would silently mix households between modules.
handling: Keep the raw row order, or add a stable key.

title: Montant has the wrong label
found: The source question is the cash received at the last distribution, but do-file 13 labels it Estimated amount from primary income source.
handling: Correct the label in do-file 13.

title: rCSI differs from the analysts' in one round
found: Mean of 4.54 against 4.79 in the raw file, the same value for 71% of households. The items match their source, so the analysts probably used another formula.
handling: No action needed unless the analysts' formula matters.

title: Households without department or phase
found: The department is missing in this round's file. The do-file fills it from the village, down from 272 to 35 households. These 35 have no Cadre Harmonisé phase, as the department is the key of that link.
handling: Find their department, if possible.

title: Dates outside the fieldwork
found: 14 interview dates fall outside the expected fieldwork, as early as 2018-01-01 for the baseline, and 10 are missing in 2020 PDM. The month is imputed for the Cadre Harmonisé link, so the phases are not affected.
handling: Do not use the interview date for durations without cleaning.

title: Duplicates and an empty record removed
found: 14 duplicate rows of 13 IDs are removed in 2021 PDM, and one household in 2023 PDM that refused the interview. One duplicated ID has rows with a different place or date; the do-file keeps the first.
handling: Done in the do-file. Check the one differing ID if needed.

title: Place names harmonised
found: 387 village names are reduced to 321, with OCHA codes attached to regions and departments, through about 300 correction lines.
handling: Done in the do-file.

title: Assistance answers on one scale
found: Do-file 13 sets all interventions to 1 = yes, 2 = no, 3 = don't know. Comparison with the original answers kept in the file gives the same Yes in all 91 tested variable and round pairs. In 2021 Annual, answers 4 and 5 become missing.
handling: Done in do-file 13. Checked on the Assistance page.

title: Food for assets recoded to cash
found: On the advice of WFP Chad, food for assets is recoded to cash for assets, as the name stayed after payments moved to cash. Food for assets therefore has no Yes.
handling: Done in do-file 13.

title: Female-headed share swings between rounds
found: The share moves between 39% and 59%. The sex recode was checked in each round against the raw labels and is right, so the swing is already in the raw files, and probably reflects the sample.
handling: Check who was interviewed before using this share as a trend.

title: Double extension of the merged file
found: The merged file is saved as WFP_Chad_2018-2023_20250423.dta.dta. The working dataset of the models reads this exact name, so renaming it needs care.
handling: Rename in both do-files if wanted.
